text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Thursday:
-- The Agricultural Ministry said in its annual report that Switzerland paid out 2.4 billion Swiss francs in direct payments to farmers in 1996, an increase of 475 million from 1995.

-- Some holders of dormant accounts in Swiss banks could easily have been found, Georg Krayer, president of the Swiss Bankers Association said. Krayer was criticising Swiss banks at a news conference to publish a list of accounts opened prior to the end of World War Two in 1945.
-- Swiss Economics Minister Jean-Pascal Delamuraz had a tumour removed from his liver.
-- The number of Swiss banks decreased in 1996 to 403 due to mergers and branch closures. The number of banking jobs in Switzerland fell 2,024, while 1,815 jobs were created abroad.

-- The University of Zurich is developping a new test for mad cow disease. The test, which is still being confirmed, would be the first one worldwide to give results within a few hours, instead of 10 days like the current test. The test would still not solve the problem of the disease's incubation time.
